I really enjoyed the game. One of its biggest strengths is how powerful and creative the builds can become once you start discovering synergies between passives and piece types. The difficulty levels provide a significant challenge, and each one also features a Boss Rush mode that pushes your strategy even further. Some bosses are extremely tough and can completely change how you approach a run, forcing you to adapt your build and think ahead rather than relying on the same strategy every time. it's a fun and challenging roguelike that becomes more rewarding the deeper you get into it (like Balatro or other games like that). Also the price is very well for what the game offer.

A really unique take on chess. It's more like Balatro than traditional chess, and I started enjoying it even more once I began connecting the dots and making builds. The Boss Rush mode and the higher difficulty levels provide a real challenge, which I personally love. As someone who enjoys difficult games that reward planning and optimization, I found there's a lot to enjoy here. Another aspect I really like is the customization. You can mix and match board skins by using different skins for the white and black tiles. And for skin pieces, my favorite is the Army skin. As for the negatives, some bosses could use clearer visual indicators for their mechanics. For example, the "Powerless" penalty reduces your combo score to 0 while you have effects in your inventory, but there isn't much visual feedback to warn you about it. If you don't carefully read the boss description, you may end up being punished without fully understanding why. I also encountered a few minor bugs during my playtime, but nothing game-breaking or crash-related.

The more I played, the more addictive the game became. Once you start discovering powerful synergies and chaining huge combos, every run feels different and keeps you coming back for more. The movement upgrade system is a really interesting idea. Upgrading each piece's movement opens up new possibilities and allows for even more creative passive combinations and strategies. My main complaint is that I often forget about the quests because they don't stand out enough in the UI. Aside from that, I had a great time with the game.

The build variety is great, and upgrading piece movement opens up a lot of interesting strategies. Once you start discovering strong synergies and chaining big combos, the game really shines. It does take some time to fully explore its mechanics, so a bit of patience is rewarded. My only minor complaint is that some quest descriptions can be a bit too wordy and could be simplified to make the information easier to read at a glance.

A surprisingly addictive roguelike take on chess. The build variety is excellent, and once the synergies start coming together, the game becomes hard to put down. Bosses keep runs interesting by forcing you to adapt your strategy, and the higher difficulties provide a real challenge. Definitely worth checking out if you enjoy strategy games and roguelikes.

As someone who considers themselves a beginner gamer and only knows how the chess pieces move on the board, I really had fun playing this game. At first, the mechanics, passives, and effects felt overwhelming, but once I took the time to learn and understand some of them, the game became very fun and satisfying. I recommend this game if you have the patience to learn and enjoy trying different combos.
This is my first time playing a roguelike game. So far so good, the game is quite catchy!!

Fun and surprisingly addictive! The game takes familiar chess-like mechanics and turns them into a fast-paced roguelike where every move matters. Building huge combo chains and discovering powerful upgrade synergies feels really rewarding. I especially like how the bosses change the rules and force you to adapt your strategy. Runs are quick, replayable, and always feel a bit different. Definitely worth trying if you enjoy strategy games with a fresh twist.

At first I thought Shattered Chess was just a clever chess gimmick, but the deeper I got, the more strategic it became. Managing resources, planning captures several moves ahead, adapting to bosses, and deciding how to develop your pieces creates a surprisingly satisfying gameplay loop. The upgradeable movement system is a very original idea and makes every run feel different. I really like it!
well optimised and i liked the unique graphic choice, and the game simply works as intented, didnt encounter any bugs

At first, i did not really understand it. But after the first hour trying new things, combos, passives, effects it started to make sense and get to be more fun. Solid 8/10. There are a few tweaks here and there, but its not too bad.

I’ve been following this game ever since the demo was released, and the full version absolutely delivers. I love the tactical complexity of the gameplay; it definitely takes a bit of patience at first, but once you understand how the mechanics work and start building synergies, it becomes extremely fun. If you like roguelikes that force you to think outside the box, this twist on chess is highly addictive!
Super catchy. Great for a quick, relaxing game session.

The first 30 minutes were a bit rough for me. There's definitely a learning curve, and it took some time before the mechanics really clicked. The tutorial helped, but I still needed a few runs to fully understand how everything worked. Once it started to make sense, though, the game became incredibly fun. The hour I spent playing flew by. I already enjoy chess and chess puzzles, but the roguelike twist adds a whole new layer of depth. Upgrading pieces, unlocking abilities, and using skills during runs makes every encounter feel fresh and engaging. If you're a fan of chess puzzles and enjoy roguelike progression systems, this is an easy recommendation.

A very cool game inspired by balatro, you can get crazy combos with the right abilities, perks and if you capture with all your pieces, don't spam just one. I like the gameplay, had to remember how to actually play chess, not just spam capturing, you have to think in advance to get some good combos. I recommend this game.

Shattered Chess proves that chess-inspired games can still feel fresh and innovative. Great strategic depth, satisfying progression, and enough variety to keep every run interesting. Easy to pick up, difficult to put down. One of the most unique indie games I've played recently.

I actually tried the demo back when it was available, and I knew right then that the concept was awesome. Now that the full game is out and I've put a few hours into it, it’s even better and super catchy. Once you start figuring out the synergies and broken upgrades, it gets incredibly addictive. It's so satisfying to hit big combos on the board. Definitely recommend it!

As someone new to roguelikes, I enjoyed the challenge Shattered Chess presents. Learning the mechanics took time, but it quickly became an enjoyable experience.
The concept of mixing chess with roguelike elements is intriguing. I appreciate the strategic depth and how each run feels fresh with the variety in upgrades and bosses.
Shattered Chess offers a unique twist on classic chess. The combination of combos and strategic decision-making keeps me coming back for more, making it quite addictive.

I found Shattered Chess to be an innovative twist on traditional chess. The strategic depth is impressive, and each run offers unique challenges and synergies to explore.
